prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Finished ARC Daily competitor character portrait in the approved glamorous CYBERPUNK illustrated aesthetic. Input1 is this person's OWN established illustrated avatar/card and supplies broad recognizable identity cues. Input2 supplies the current NVIDIA CITADEL world and polished painted/inked character aesthetic ONLY, never CPMP's face, beard, ponytail, chair, name or costume. Faces must be clearly REDRAWN and IDEALIZED: handsome sculpted painted facial planes, groomed features, flattering healthy complexion, appropriate adult age, expressive eyes. No photographic face pasted onto armor, no copied pores/imperfections, no anime or young generic actor likeness. Glamour preserves adult age and characteristic features; no de-aging everyone into twenties. Every face, hand, cloth and metal surface shares one confident cinematic graphic-novel illustration medium.

NVIDIA Citadel world: enormous black/graphite GPU rack towers, emerald cooling loops, fan walls, angular command decks and snowy mountains, warm amber light, restrained crimson costume accents. Worthy charismatic competitors, not evil villains. Distinct personal pose, equipment silhouette and narrative function rather than repeated generic engineer or mastermind throne. Hardware/powers/roles are editorial fantasy, not claims about actual techniques or employment roles. Huge identifiable graphics cards, green PCB edges, cooling fans, silver heatsinks, copper pipes and geometric multicolored ARC-square screens. Open unconventional cyber headgear can be weird and bulky while leaving most face visible.

Portrait5:7, ideally1500x2100, full bleed. Head through waist/upper thighs, face near upper third, whole helmet, hands and key apparatus inside frame, top strip and bottom quarter calmer for later programmatic baseball-card overlays. Art ONLY. No text, names, aliases, letters, digits, card frames, badges, ranks, scores, captions, watermark or typography. Do not copy CPMP engraving from input2. One main character only. GAL KAPLUN — THE GRID PILOT. Reimagine source's own illustrated adult male avatar, preserving swept chestnut-brown hair, long slim face, distinctive narrow moustache/light stubble, sunglasses perched above forehead and easy knowing smile. A handsome charismatic adult cyber engineer/adventurer with bright intelligent eyes, elegant nose and painted sculpted facial planes. No anime, no full heavy beard, no copied CPMP face.
Entirely different narrative composition and equipment: Gal leans casually over the control bars of an absurdly powerful GPU HOVER-SKIMMER in the NVIDIA Citadel's high landing hangar. Upper-body portrait, his head/torso and the front half of his machine dominate. One glove steadies an asymmetric control yoke while the other adjusts a physical multicolored ARC-grid navigation panel mounted on a swivel. The machine's nose is an enormous OPEN GRAPHICS-CARD ENGINE: exposed green PCB blades, two huge downward-angled turbine cooling fans, horizontal silver heatsink stacks, copper manifolds and glowing green suspension coils. This is a recognizable ludicrous wearable/rideable GPU machine, not a normal motorcycle with an arbitrary glowing light. Convey the tableau of a brilliant, relaxed field operator ready to depart, NOT a seated command throne or another identical map-table tactician.
Costume: deep CRIMSON leather utility flight jacket under asymmetrical GRAPHITE/SILVER shoulder bracing, emerald illuminated seams and modular ARC grid wrist controller. Distinct open pilot helmet with swept-back silver side fins, exposed ear mechanisms, copper cheek communicator and thick forehead-mounted flip-up cyber sunglasses (echoing his source's glasses) leaving both eyes, moustache and smile visible. Brown hair emerges naturally from top/rear of open helmet. Lower half of frame includes part of enormous GPU engine and control bars, no tiny full-body scene. Behind: towering black/green NVIDIA rack towers inside an open angular hangar door, snow mountains and emerald-lit landing gantry at sunset. Glamorous, playful confidence and clearly hand-painted human face, not an exact snapshot or generic space marine. No weapons, no extra people, no lettering.

review: Preserves Gal's own illustrated swept hair, narrow moustache/stubble, long face and raised sunglasses motifs. Crimson flight jacket, open finned cyber headset and hands on GPU hover-skimmer controls distinguish him from other NVIDIA characters. Painted adult face, giant cooling-engine foreground, emerald citadel and no labels or card frame.
